items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: we used to say a lot of the licks that Ernie put into “Every Day” we’d already like set those things, and he wrote them in.

ctx.x: Do you know that that “Every Day” started out as a head tune. Do you remember when Joe Williams joined the band and we took that southern swing? And I remember because
we used to say a lot of the licks that Ernie put into “Every Day” we’d already like set those things, and he wrote them in.

Right. And then there were two songs that were heads from “Jump City”: “I Got a Gal”— “Roll ‘Em Pete” and “Shake, Rattle and Roll.” Not a note of music written for either of those full fledged arrangements. I mean the audience would never know the difference. That was going back to the old days in the best way possible — totally from the head. Then there was recording that we did, now this was, this was off the subject of Joe Williams, remember when they had the M Squad, that detective story on television? They…
